correctness.rationale: The composite objective has positive-definite exact Hessian \(I_2\) and convex \(|x_1+x_2|\). The unique P-proximal first direction and H-conjugate full-rank second direction satisfy explicit exact optimality equations. Two strict scalar subdifferential tests force \(\alpha_2=0\), the first scalar quadratic determines \(\alpha_1=D/K\), and the third line has \(\alpha_3=1\). The unique joint minimizer has the independent subgradient certificate at \((1,-1)\), yielding exact value \(-1\). Algebra gives \(R_N=\delta^2(1+h^2)^2/[2(1+h^2\delta^2)]\) and \(N^2R_N\to25/2\). Exact-rational package verifier checks finite representative values; it is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating paper explicitly uses two decoupled one-dimensional local proximal solves to approximate a two-dimensional joint nonsmooth model. The exact relative model decrease, rather than correctness or vague stability, is a natural indicator of solution quality. The theorem quantifies a severe obstruction: a family with identity Hessian and the prescribed \(A^{\mathsf T}A\) preconditioner admits positive but vanishing \(\Theta(N^{-2})\) relative model decrease despite an entire two-dimensional trial space and an extra ray refinement. It indicates why guarantee-driven implementations may need a coupled small-dimensional solve or condition-dependent accuracy control. No broad convergence theorem or algorithmic failure is claimed.
